guide.description: uniq collapses consecutive duplicate lines into one. It only looks at ADJACENT lines — it has no idea two matching lines exist if something else sits between them — which is exactly why you sort first. -c prefixes each remaining line with how many times it occurred.

flags.desc: prefix each line with its occurrence count

exercises.title: Collapse duplicates

exercises.title: Put it together: rank by frequency
exercises.task: You now know awk, sort, and uniq -c individually. Chain them, then pipe into sort -n so the codes come out ordered from least to most frequent.
